column1: # authorization macro (authorize.sql) on a hardened engine must reject and
# what it must let through, with DuckDB 2.0.0 and the extensions of the image.
# One case per line, four fields separated by a tab: ID, OUTCOME, KIND, SQL.
# OUTCOME is BLOCK (rejected by the macro), PERM (refused by DuckDB: no file
# or network access), LOCK (refused by DuckDB: configuration locked), ERR (any
# error) or OK (no error). KIND Q sends the SQL to the engine as the text of
# one query, the way a client pushes a query down (FROM r.query('...')); KIND
# C runs it in the client on the attached database "r", so the client sends
# its own queries (catalog, uploads). The cases run in this order in one
# session. The SQL is ASCII; placeholders stand for other characters: {nl}
# line feed, {tab}, {vt} vertical tab, {nbsp} U+00A0, {zwsp} U+200B, {idsp}
# U+3000, {kelvin} U+212A KELVIN SIGN, {longs} U+017F LONG S, {cyr_a} U+0430
# and {cyr_u} U+0443 (Cyrillic look-alikes of a and u). Lines starting with #
# Tables and other objects that the cases create are named authz_* and
# A table for the cases below.

column4: CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE r.authz_t AS SELECT range AS i, 'row ' || range AS s FROM range(1000)

column1: # The Quack server: quack_* in any spelling DuckDB accepts.

column4: WITH s AS (SELECT * FROM quack_stop('quack:0.0.0.0:9494')) SELECT * FROM s
PREPARE authz_p1 AS SELECT * FROM quack_stop('quack:0.0.0.0:9494')
CALL quack_serve('quack:0.0.0.0:9999', token = 'attacker-token-0123456789', allow_other_hostname = true, disable_ssl = true)
SELECT 'x' AS a, * FROM quack_stop('quack:0.0.0.0:9494') -- trailing
SELECT 1{nl}UNION ALL SELECT count(*) FROM quack_stop('quack:0.0.0.0:9494'::VARCHAR)

column1: # SQL that is not in the text of the query: built at run time, read from

column4: SELECT * FROM query/* a /* b */ c */('SELECT 1')
REGISTER EXTERNAL RESOURCE 'authz_squat' AS authz_res2 FROM MAP {}

column4: SELECT name, secret_string FROM duckdb_secrets(redact := false)

column1: # Writing files: with external access off, DuckDB still allows its temp
# directory and the files of the attached databases (the database file and
# its WAL). IMPORT DATABASE would run what lands there.

column4: COPY (SELECT 1 AS x) TO '/tmp/.tmp/schema.sql' (FORMAT csv, HEADER false, QUOTE '')
COPY (SELECT 1 AS x) TO (current_setting('temp_directory') || '/schema.sql') (FORMAT csv, HEADER false, QUOTE '')
COPY (SELECT 'garbage' AS x) TO '/data/engine.duckdb' (FORMAT csv, HEADER false, USE_TMP_FILE false)
COPY (SELECT 1 AS x) TO '/data/engine.duckdb.wal' (FORMAT csv, USE_TMP_FILE false)
COPY (SELECT '.print injected') TO '/proc/self/fd/0' (FORMAT csv, HEADER false, QUOTE '')
COPY FROM DATABASE memory TO memory
ATTACH TO NEW TEMPORARY EXTERNAL RESOURCE 'authz_squat' AS authz_res3

column4: SELECT 1 AS copy_count, 2 AS exported, 3 AS importer, 4 AS reconnect
